---
title: "IRT dimensionality and DIF checks for the mental rotation task"
---

Follow-up to `02_fit_irt.qmd`. Starting from the response matrix of the paper's scalar 2PL model, this
(1) tests the single-factor assumption against models with a separate 3D factor, and
(2) tests each item class for differential item functioning (DIF) across the four datasets.
Results are saved to `models/` and reported in `mrot_paper/extra_analyses.qmd`.

```{r}
library(here)
library(readr)
source(here("helper", "irt_checks.R"))

dat <- load_mrot_irt_data(here("models/mrot/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items/mrot_2pl_f1_scalar.rds"))
```

## Check: rebuilt scalar model against the saved one

The rebuilt model should reproduce the scalar 2PL fit in `models/mrot_anova.rds` (BIC ≈ 43571).

```{r}
m_uni <- fit_mrot(dat, "uni", quadpts = 61)
saved <- read_rds(here("models/mrot_anova.rds")) |>
  filter(model_set == "multigroup_dataset", itemtype == "2pl", invariance == "scalar")
tibble(source = c("rebuilt", "saved"),
       logLik = c(m_uni@Fit$logLik, saved$logLik),
       BIC = c(m_uni@Fit$BIC, saved$BIC))
```

## Dimensionality

All models are multigroup (four datasets), scalar-invariant (parameters equal across datasets and
across the instances of an item class), with the paper's priors and guessing fixed at .5.
The multidimensional models use 31 quadrature points per dimension, so the one-factor model is refit
at 31 points for a like-for-like comparison.

```{r}
dim_models <- list(
  "One factor"                       = fit_mrot(dat, "uni", quadpts = 31),
  "Two correlated factors (2D, 3D)"  = fit_mrot(dat, "two", quadpts = 31),
  "General + 3D-specific factor"     = fit_mrot(dat, "bifactor", quadpts = 31)
)

dim_fit <- imap(dim_models, \(m, label) fit_summary(m, label)) |> list_rbind() |>
  mutate(d_BIC = BIC - min(BIC))

# correlation between the 2D and 3D factors in each dataset
two <- as_tibble(mod2values(dim_models[["Two correlated factors (2D, 3D)"]])) |>
  filter(class == "GroupPars") |>
  select(group, name, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = value)
dim_cor <- two |> transmute(group, r_2d_3d = COV_21 / sqrt(COV_11 * COV_22))

write_rds(list(fit = dim_fit, cor = dim_cor), here("models/mrot_dim.rds"), compress = "gz")
dim_fit
dim_cor
```

## Differential item functioning

Each of the 12 item classes is freed in turn (slope and intercept free across datasets, df = 6) and
compared with the all-invariant model by likelihood ratio. Likelihoods are unpenalised, because the
priors used for the paper's models shrink freed parameters and make the likelihood ratio unreliable.
DIF is run under the one-factor model (the paper's) and the two-factor model (which fits better).

```{r}
dif_uni <- class_dif(dat, "uni", quadpts = 61)
dif_two <- class_dif(dat, "two", quadpts = 31)
write_rds(list(uni = dif_uni, two = dif_two), here("models/mrot_dif.rds"), compress = "gz")

dif_uni |> select(-est)
dif_two |> select(-est)
```
